summary: 翼龙已灭绝，研究者只能从化石和模型反推其飞行方式。文章追踪研究团队怎样重建翼部及特殊翼骨，再用可操纵模型检验对翼龙飞行的设想。

paragraphs.brief: 凯特・托马斯遇到了马修・威尔金森教授他建造了一个生命体积模型来找出这个史前掠食者是怎么从地上下来的
sentences: Is that a bird in the sky?
那是天上的鸟吗？
A plane?
飞机？
No, it’s a pterosaur.
不，这是一只巨龙。
Kate Thomas meets Professor Matthew Wilkinson, who built a life-size model to find out how this prehistoric predator ever got off the ground.
凯特・托马斯遇到了马修・威尔金森教授他建造了一个生命体积模型来找出这个史前掠食者是怎么从地上下来的

paragraphs.brief: 翼龙生存于距今约 2.2 亿年前的三叠纪，一直延续到约 6,500 万年前的白垩纪末期；当时南美洲与非洲分离，南大西洋逐渐形成。
sentences: Pterosaurs existed from the Triassic period, 220 million years ago, to the end of the Cretaceous period, 65 million years ago, when South America pulled away from Africa and the South Atlantic was formed.
翼龙生存于距今约 2.2 亿年前的三叠纪，一直延续到约 6,500 万年前的白垩纪末期；当时南美洲与非洲分离，南大西洋逐渐形成。
They are among the least understood of all the extinct reptiles that once spent their lives in the skies while the dinosaurs dominated the land.
他们是最不了解的爬行动物曾经在天空度过生命而恐龙统治着这片土地
Pterosaurs had no feathers, but at least part of their bodies was covered in hair, not unlike bats.
野生动物没有羽毛，但至少他们身体的一部分被头发覆盖，不像蝙蝠。
Some believe this is an indication they were warm-blooded.
有些人认为这是他们被热血淋淋的迹象。

Researchers also debate whether pterosaurs travelled on the ground by walking on their hind legs, like birds, or by using all fours, relying on their three-toed front feet as well as their four-toed rear feet.
研究者们还争论说，恐龙是靠后腿行走，如鸟类，还是靠三脚前脚和四脚后脚行走。

paragraphs.brief: 这里不仅发现了数百颗两栖动物的化石* 和其他爬行动物，考古学家们也发现了一些保存良好的龙虾。
sentences: Pterosaurs were vertebrates, meaning they were the first species possessing backbones to become airborne, but scientists have never quite understood their flight technique.
白龙是脊椎动物，意思是它们是最先拥有骨骼的物种成为空中，但科学家从来没有完全理解他们的飞行技术。
How, they wondered, did such a heavy creature ever manage to take off?
他们不知道，这样一个重物是怎么起飞的？
How could a wing that appears to have been supported by fine, hollow bones have carried one into the sky?
一个看起来有精美空心骨支撑的翅膀怎么会把一只带入天空呢？
Then came the discovery of a site in Brazil’s Araripe basin.
之后在巴西阿拉里佩盆地发现了一个地点。
Here, not only were hundreds of fossils of amphibians* and other reptiles found, but archaeologists unearthed a number of very well-preserved pterosaurs.
这里不仅发现了数百颗两栖动物的化石* 和其他爬行动物，考古学家们也发现了一些保存良好的龙虾。
The anhanguera — a fish-eating subspecies of pterosaur that ruled the skies in the Cretaceous period — was among them.
其中一个是阿汉古拉——在白鲸时期统治天空的食鱼亚类。
With a wingspan of up to 12 metres, they would have made an amazing sight in the sky — had any human been there to witness it.
如果有12米长的翅膀，他们就会在天空中看到一个惊人的景象——如果有任何人在那里见证。
‘I’ve been studying pterosaurs for about eight years now,’ says Dr Matthew Wilkinson, a professor of zoology at Cambridge University.
说马修·威尔金森博士剑桥大学动物学教授：“我学了八年龙了。”
With an anhanguera fossil as his model, Wilkinson began gradually reconstructing its skeletal structure in his Cambridge studio.
威尔金森开始在剑桥演播室逐步重建骨骼结构
The probability of finding three-dimensional pterosaur fossils anywhere is slim.
在任何地方找到三维天龙化石的概率微乎其微
‘That was quite a find,’ he says.
他说：这是个不错的发现。
‘Their bones are usually crushed to dust.’
骨头通常被粉碎。
Once the structure was complete, it inspired him to make a robot version as a way to understand the animal’s locomotion.
一旦结构完成，他就会被启发制作一个机器人版本，来理解动物的运动。
With a team of model-makers, he has built a remote-controlled pterosaur in his studio.
他与一组模特制造者在他的工作室里建造了一个遥控的巨龙
‘Fossils show just how large these creatures were.
浮标显示这些生物有多大
I’ve always been interested in how they managed to launch themselves, so I thought the real test would be to actually build one and fly it.’
我一直很想知道他们是如何自己发动的所以我觉得真正的测试就是建造一个飞翔的

paragraphs.brief: 威尔金森并不孤单地渴望重新创造史前的野兽。
sentences: Wilkinson hasn’t been alone in his desire to recreate a prehistoric beast.
威尔金森并不孤单地渴望重新创造史前的野兽。

Swiss scientists recently announced they had built an amphibious robot that could walk on land and swim in water using the sort of backbone movements that must have been employed by the first creatures to crawl from the sea.
瑞士科学家最近宣布，他们建造了一个两栖机器人，可以步行到陆地上，在水中游泳，使用脊椎运动，而这种运动一定是第一批生物从海上爬出来的。
But Wilkinson had the added complication of working out his beast’s flight technique.
但威尔金森的飞行技巧却变得更为复杂

Unlike those of bats or flying squirrels, pterosaur wings — soft, stretchy membranes of skin tissue — are thought to have reached from the chest to the ankle, reinforced by fibres that stiffened the wing and prevented tearing.
与蝙蝠或飞松鼠不同的是，据认为，皮肤组织软软、伸展性膜从胸部伸到脚踝，并用纤维加固，使翅膀僵硬，防止撕裂。
Smaller subspecies flapped their wings during takeoff.
小型子物种在起飞时翅膀被击碎了
That may have explained the creatures’ flexibility, but it did not answer the most pressing question: how did such heavy animals manage to launch themselves into the sky?
这也许解释了动物的灵活性，但并没有回答最紧迫的问题：这些重动物是如何射入天空的？
Working with researchers in London and Berlin, Wilkinson began to piece together the puzzle.
威尔金森与伦敦和柏林的研究人员合作开始拼凑出谜题

paragraphs.brief: 风隧道的初步试验证明了这一点——具有远方成形类固醇的巨型龙虾模型不仅能够滑翔，而且具有敏捷性，尽管其尺寸很大。
sentences: It emerged that the anhanguera had an elongated limb called the pteroid.
发现安汉古拉有长肢叫做类固醇
It had previously been thought the pteroid pointed towards the shoulder of the creature and supported a soft forewing in front of the arm.
以前曾认为，这种类固醇指向该生物的肩膀，支持在手臂前进行柔软的织造。
But if that were the case, the forewing would have been too small and ineffectual for flight.
但如果是这样的话，开关会太小，没有效果，无法飞行。

However, to the surprise of many scientists, fossils from the Araripe basin showed the pteroid possibly faced the opposite way, creating a much greater forewing that would have caught the air, working in the same way as the flaps on the wings of an aeroplane.
然而，令许多科学家感到惊讶的是，来自阿拉里佩盆地的化石展示出这种类固醇可能正相反地面对的情况，制造出一个比飞机翼上的螺旋状物更能接上空气的发芽。
So, with both feet on the ground, the anhanguera might have simply faced into the wind, spread its wings and risen up into the sky.
所以，两只脚都躺在地上，Anhanguera可能只是面对风，展开翅膀，升到天空。
Initial trials in wind tunnels proved the point — models of pterosaurs with forward-facing pteroids were not only adept at gliding, but were agile flyers in spite of their size.
风隧道的初步试验证明了这一点——具有远方成形类固醇的巨型龙虾模型不仅能够滑翔，而且具有敏捷性，尽管其尺寸很大。
‘This high-lift capability would have significantly reduced the minimum flight speed, allowing even the largest forms to take off without difficulty,’ Wilkinson says.
威尔金森说，即使最大的表格也能毫无困难地起飞：“这种高升降能力将大大降低最低飞行速度。”
‘It would have enabled them to glide very slowly and may have been instrumental in the evolution of large size by the pterosaurs.’
这会让他们滑翔得非常缓慢，并且可能有助于巨型龙的大规模进化。

paragraphs.brief: "我们不得不把它飞行至今没有头。"
sentences: Resting in the grass at the test site near Cambridge, the robot model’s wings ripple in the wind.
在剑桥附近的试验场休息机器人模型的翅膀在风中摇晃
In flight, the flexible membrane, while much stiffer than the real thing, allows for a smooth takeoff and landing.
在飞行中，柔性膜虽然比真实物质硬得多，但能够顺利起飞和着陆。
But the model has been troubled by other mechanical problems.
但模型一直受到其他机械问题的困扰。
‘Unlike an aircraft, which is stabilised by the tail wing at the back, the model is stabilised by its head, which means it can start spinning around.
不像飞机后面的尾翼稳定下来模型头部稳定下来也就是说它可以开始旋转了
That’s the most problematic bit as far as we’re concerned,’ Wilkinson says.
威尔金森说，这是我们最有问题的一点。
‘We’ve had to take it flying without the head so far.’
"我们不得不把它飞行至今没有头。"
When it flies with its head attached, Wilkinson will finally have proved his point.
威尔金森终于证明了他的观点

paragraphs.brief: 那么动物学家接下来要做什么呢？
sentences: So what’s next for the zoologist — perhaps a full-size Tyrannosaurus rex?
那么动物学家接下来要做什么呢？
‘No,’ he tells me.
他告诉我,
‘We’re desperate to build really big pterosaurs — creatures with even greater wingspans, weighing a quarter of a ton.
我们急切地想造出真正的巨型龙 —— 翅膀更宽，体重为四分之一吨的生物。

But,’ he adds, just as one begins to fear for the safety and stress levels of pilots landing nearby at Cambridge City Airport, ‘it’s more likely we’ll start off with one of the smaller, flapping pterosaurs.’
”他补充说，正如人们开始担心降落在剑桥市机场的飞行员的安全和压力水平一样，“我们更有可能从一个更小的、拍打的巨人开始。
This is certainly more reassuring.
这肯定更令人放心。
Let’s hope he is content to leave it at that.
让我们希望他满足于离开它。

items.en: They are classed as ________, which were capable of flight, although, unlike modern species, they had some ____ (Q28), which is evidence of their having had warm blood.
items.zh: 翼龙属于能飞行的 ________。与现存的同类动物不同，它们身上还有一些 ________（Q28），这表明它们是温血动物。
items.why: 空格前是 are classed as,意思是“被归类为”。原文直接说辟龙是 extinct reptiles,所以选 reptiles 疏行动物。注意不能选 dinosaurs,因为原文说 dinosaurs dominated the land,而贾龙是在天空生活的 extinct reptiles,并不是恐龙。

items.en: They are classed as ____ (Q27), which were capable of flight, although, unlike modern species, they had some ________, which is evidence of their having had warm blood.
items.zh: 翼龙属于能飞行的 ________（Q27）。与现存的同类动物不同，它们身上还有一些 ________，这表明它们是温血动物。
items.why: 回到对应内容“野生动物没有羽毛，但至少他们身体的一部分被头发覆盖，不像蝙蝠”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: There are two theories as to how they moved on land: perhaps with all their feet or by using their ________ only.
items.zh: 关于翼龙如何在陆地上移动，有人认为它们四足并用，也有人认为它们只用 ________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“研究者们还争论说，恐龙是靠后腿行走，如鸟类，还是靠三脚前脚和四脚后脚行走”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Another mystery has concerned the ability of the pterosaur to fly despite its immense ________, and the fact that the bones making up the wing did not have great ____ (Q31) Thanks to reptile fossils found in Brazil, we now know that the subspecies known as anhanguera had wings that were 12 metres across and that it mainly survived on ____ (Q32)
items.zh: 翼龙的 ________ 如此之大，翼骨的 ________（Q31） 又不高，究竟怎样飞起来也是个谜。巴西发现的化石表明，名为安杭古翼龙的亚种翼展达12米，主要以 ________（Q32） 为食。
items.why: 题干中的 despite its immense…对应原文 such a heavy creature, heavy 表示“重的",名词形式对应选项 weight 重量。所以答案是 J weight。

items.en: Another mystery has concerned the ability of the pterosaur to fly despite its immense ____ (Q30), and the fact that the bones making up the wing did not have great ________ Thanks to reptile fossils found in Brazil, we now know that the subspecies known as anhanguera had wings that were 12 metres across and that it mainly survived on ____ (Q32)
items.zh: 翼龙的 ________（Q30） 如此之大，翼骨的 ________ 又不高，究竟怎样飞起来也是个谜。巴西发现的化石表明，名为安杭古翼龙的亚种翼展达12米，主要以 ________（Q32） 为食。
items.why: 原文说贾龙翅膀由 fine, hollow bones 支撑，即“细而中空的骨头”,这暗示骨头看起来不够结实。题干改写为 the bones…did not have great…,应填 strength 强度 / 力量。所以选 strength。

items.en: Another mystery has concerned the ability of the pterosaur to fly despite its immense ____ (Q30), and the fact that the bones making up the wing did not have great ____ (Q31) Thanks to reptile fossils found in Brazil, we now know that the subspecies known as anhanguera had wings that were 12 metres across and that it mainly survived on ________
items.zh: 翼龙的 ________（Q30） 如此之大，翼骨的 ________（Q31） 又不高，究竟怎样飞起来也是个谜。巴西发现的化石表明，名为安杭古翼龙的亚种翼展达12米，主要以 ________ 为食。
items.why: 题干中的 mainly survived on 意思是“主要以…为食 /生存”。原文说 fish-eating,即“吃鱼的”,所以答案是 Bfish。

groups.label: 选词填空
groups.instructionsZh: 阅读带空格的中译，回想正确词项及其字母。

items.en: It is rare to find a fossil of a pterosaur that clearly shows its skeleton.
items.zh: 能清楚显示翼龙骨架的化石很少见。
items.why: 原文写道“在任何地方找到三维天龙化石的概率微乎其微”，支持题干所说的“能清楚显示翼龙骨架的化石很少见”。

items.en: The reason for building the model was to prove pterosaurs flew for long distances.
items.zh: 制作模型是为了证明翼龙能长距离飞行。
items.why: 题干说建模型是为了证明翼龙 flew for long distances 长距离飞行。但原文说目的是了解 locomotion 运动方式，尤其是 how they managed to launch themselves 它们如何起飞。原文目的不是证明长距离飞行，因此与原文矛盾，答案是 NO。

items.en: It is possible that pterosaur species achieved their wing size as a result of the pteroid.
items.zh: 翼龙的翅膀可能正是因为有翼骨，才能长到那样大。
items.why: 题干中的 lt is possible 对应原文 may have been,都表示“可能"。原文说 pteroid 的朝向形成了更大的前相，并且这种高升力能力可能推动了收龙大型化的进化。题干说机龙的要展 /翅膀尺寸可能与 pteroid 有关，与原文一致，所以答案是 YES。

items.en: Wilkinson has made several unsuccessful replicas of the pterosaur’s head.
items.zh: 威尔金森制作翼龙头部模型的几次尝试都失败了。
items.why: 团队目前只能让模型在不带头部的情况下试飞。由这个限制无法得知威尔金森曾制作多少个头部复制件，也不能确定多个成品都失败了。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: What was Professor Wilkinson’s main problem, according to the third paragraph?
items.zh: 第三段说威尔金森教授的主要问题是什么？
correct: Large pterosaurs were not able to take off like other flying animals.
大型翼龙无法像其他会飞的动物那样起飞。

items.en: What did Professor Wilkinson discover about a bone in pterosaurs called a pteroid?
items.zh: 对于翼龙身上特有的翼骨（pteroid），威尔金森教授发现了什么？
correct: It was in an unexpected position.
这块骨头所在的位置出乎意料。

items.en: According to the writer, the main problem with the remote-controlled ‘pterosaur’ is that
items.zh: 据作者说，遥控的"pterosaur"的主要问题是
correct: it cannot be controlled when its head is attached.
一旦给模型装上头部，就无法操控它了。

items.en: What does ‘it’ in the last sentence refer to?
items.zh: 最后一句中`它 ' 指的是什么？
correct: 威尔金森想要建立模型

pairs: evidence of their having had warm blood
它们是温血动物的迹象

points: 团队目前只能让模型在不带头部的情况下试飞。由这个限制无法得知威尔金森曾制作多少个头部复制件，也不能确定多个成品都失败了。
回到对应内容“研究者们还争论说，恐龙是靠后腿行走，如鸟类，还是靠三脚前脚和四脚后脚行走”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: Kate Thomas meets Professor Matthew Wilkinson, ….
“who built a life-size model to find out how this prehistoric predator ever got off the ground”修饰前面的 Wilkinson。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 Wilkinson，再把修饰信息接回主句。
In flight, the flexible membrane, …, allows for a smooth takeoff and landing.
连接词 while 引出“while much stiffer than the real thing”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
